- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true by >5%), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +2% above true peak for next 3–7 days.
- If sentiment is negative (≤ 0.33) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive forecasts are above true, adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overreacts to sentiment shifts; use sentiment-weighted smoothing: if sentiment > 0.67, apply 70% weight to recent history; if < 0.33, apply 30%.
- If sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.33/1.00), model tends to overfit short-term noise; dampen forecast by 1–2% for next 2–4 days.
